jojo.title: Meet jojo
jojo.body: Your assistant lives here. It reacts to what you do — a dance when an application goes out, a nod when a task is done — and follows your pointer around the page.
jojo.task: Tap jojo, or draw a circle on it.

moves.title: Every move, and how to draw it
moves.body: This button lists all of jojo’s moves, each with the stroke that plays it — a swipe up to hop, a Z to doze off — and credits the artist of the 3D model.

runtime.title: Where your records live
runtime.body: “Saved here” is browser storage: a database inside this browser, on this machine — nothing is sent anywhere and nothing syncs. The other tiles say whether a model is connected and offer to move everything to another device. Each one opens where it is set up.

applications.title: Your applications
applications.body: One record per job: the position, the employer, its stage and your notes. Deadlines, interviews and documents all hang off it, so nothing is typed twice.

layout.title: A board or a table
layout.body: The same records, two ways. The board shows the stages as columns; the table sorts and searches. The choice is in the address, so a link opens the way you left it.

records.title: Six stages, and jojo cheers each one
records.body: Draft, Submitted, Screen, Interview, Offer, Closed. On the board, drag a card to its next column: jojo dances when a draft goes out, powers up for an interview and leaps for an offer. Every move undoes.

keywords.title: Keywords are your tags
keywords.body: One set of tags across applications, reminders and the vault. Tag a record from the tag button on its row, add a new keyword with +, and right-click a chip to rename, recolour or delete it.
keywords.task: Pick a keyword to filter by it.

new.title: Make anything
new.body: New makes an application, a reminder, a calendar entry, a drafted message, a saved link or a saved posting. The n key opens it from anywhere you are not typing.

new-menu.title: Nothing is saved until you save
new-menu.body: Each of these opens its own form. Closing a half-filled form costs nothing but the typing.

search.title: The fastest way in
search.body: Search every application, reminder and calendar entry, jump to any page — including the ones the sidebar does not list — or run one of the app’s own operations.
search.task: Press ⌘K (Ctrl K), or click the search bar.

palette.title: Type to find anything
palette.body: A role, an organisation or a stage. The arrow keys pick, Enter goes.
palette.task: Close it with Esc when you are done looking.

calendar.title: Every date in one place
calendar.body: Deadlines, interviews and follow-ups are one kind of record, so one entry shows on the calendar, on the dashboard and on its application. Drag one to another day to reschedule it.

vault.title: The vault
vault.body: Everything a job search piles up besides applications: reminders, saved links, files, the snippets you paste into every form, the people you know, and a few tools.

files.title: Files, previewed in place
files.body: Drop in a CV, a statement or a posting. PDFs, images, text and saved web pages open right here, and each file can carry a note and keywords. Files are stored in this browser, not uploaded.
files.task: Click a file to preview it.

file-viewer.title: The preview
file-viewer.body: Read it without leaving the page. With the document reader connected (Settings), the assistant can read what is inside it too.

tools.title: Tools
tools.body: A calculator, basic or scientific, that keeps a history of its sums — and a PDF editor.

pdf.title: PDF tools
pdf.body: Merge several PDFs into one, reorder or delete pages, and mark one up — all inside this browser, so no document is ever uploaded. Drop PDFs straight onto this panel.

scout.title: Job scout
scout.body: Saved searches that watch job boards for you.

pipelines.title: Pipelines
pipelines.body: Each pipeline is a search on a board (HigherEdJobs, AcademicCareers and others). It runs on a schedule or when you press Run now; what it finds waits as suggestions you approve or discard, and an approved one becomes a draft application.

statistics.title: Statistics
statistics.body: How your search is going, counted from your own records.

stats.title: Rates, with honest error bars
stats.body: Response and interview rates, a funnel and a week-by-week chart — each rate with the range it could really be, since a handful of applications is a small sample. It follows the role filter in the top bar.

graph.title: The knowledge graph
graph.body: Every record — applications, employers, people, dates, files — is a node, and how they connect is the edges. Ask a question in words or build one, and the matching records light up. It is not in the sidebar; ⌘K gets you here.

chat.title: Chat with jojo
chat.body: The assistant can find, add and update your records with the app’s own tools, and asks before it changes anything unless you tell it not to. It needs a model — which is the next step.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Models, the document reader, keywords, your data — and every gesture jojo knows.

model.title: Connect a model
model.body: Pick where the assistant’s model runs. A local server — vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or Ollama — takes its address and keeps your records on this machine. OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), OpenRouter, Groq or NVIDIA take an API key. Test connection checks it before anything is saved.

reader.title: Let it read your documents
reader.body: MarkItDown turns PDFs, Word files, decks and spreadsheets into text the assistant can read. Copy the two commands here into a terminal — one installs it, one starts it — then press Test connection.

keyword-manager.title: Manage your keywords
keyword-manager.body: Add keywords, rename them, give them any colour, or delete them. A rename carries everywhere the keyword is shown.

backup.title: Keep a backup
backup.body: Clearing the browser takes your records with it, so export a backup now and then — one file with everything. jojo flexes when you do.

done.title: That’s the tour
done.body: Undo is ⌘Z anywhere, and every change is listed in the audit log at the foot of Settings. The guide covers every screen in turn — How to use, in the top bar — and the tour is there to take again.

overlay.endLabel: End the tour (your place is kept)
